- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If model consistently forecasts below 60% of recent 18-day average, apply upward bias (e.g., +1.5–3%) to reflect mean reversion toward recent highs.
- When sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates continuation; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for momentum bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility; increase final 5–7 days of forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for lagged sentiment effects.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak or trough to align with sentiment momentum.
